items.name: ai-chat
items.displayName: AI Chat (Azure OpenAI + App Service + Cosmos DB)
items.description: A chat API on App Service that calls an Azure OpenAI gpt-5-mini deployment and persists conversations in serverless Cosmos DB. All access is keyless via managed identity.
items.what: A chat API on App Service that calls an Azure OpenAI gpt-5-mini deployment and stores conversation history in serverless Cosmos DB. Access to both OpenAI and Cosmos is keyless via the app's managed identity (local auth disabled). Dev is cheap; prod is zone-redundant with higher model throughput.
items.why: Conversational AI is the most requested GenAI pattern. This wires the three pieces every chatbot needs - a model endpoint, a stateless app tier, and durable conversation storage - with keyless security and pay-per-use billing that matches spiky chat traffic.
potentialUseCases: A customer-support or internal helpdesk chatbot
A product/document Q&A assistant (extend with retrieval from the AI landing zone)
A copilot embedded in an existing web app
A GenAI prototype you harden to production with the prod profile

reliability: Zone-redundant App Service plan in prod
Cosmos DB serverless with Session consistency and automatic failover priority
Stateless app tier - conversation state lives in Cosmos
security: Keyless access: managed identity to Azure OpenAI and Cosmos (local auth disabled)
TLS 1.2 minimum across all tiers, HTTPS-only app
Custom subdomain on the OpenAI account for Entra token auth
costOptimization: Cosmos serverless - pay per request unit, ideal for spiky chat load
Pay-as-you-go token billing on the model deployment
Dev uses Basic app plan and low TPM capacity
operationalExcellence: Telemetry in Application Insights + Log Analytics
Model name/version and TPM capacity are parameters
IaC with dev/prod parameter files
performanceEfficiency: Provisioned TPM capacity tuned per environment
Cosmos serverless scales throughput automatically
Premium v3 app compute in prod

items.name: event-streaming-analytics
items.description: Event Hubs ingestion, a Stream Analytics job shaping events to a curated lake, a Functions hot-path consumer, and Cosmos DB serving - all keyless.
items.what: Devices and apps publish to an Event Hubs namespace. A Stream Analytics job reads one consumer group, applies a windowed transformation, and lands curated Parquet in an ADLS-style container.
